name: British top-boost style (EL84 pair, no feedback)
notes: 60s British 'chime' style: bright, jangly, breaks up early and sweetly, very touch-sensitive. Its key features: EL84 power tubes, a tube rectifier (lots of sag), and NO global feedback loop (so there is no feedback block). Path: V1 -> volume -> top boost stage -> treble/bass circuit -> phase inverter with a 'cut' control -> 2x EL84. FROM SCHEMATICS (fairly sure): EL84 pair, no global negative feedback, tube rectifier, a cut control after the phase inverter, 12AX7 preamp stages. The treble/bass circuit is the tone stack block's top_boost style: 50 pF, 22 nF, 22 nF, 100k, 1M log treble and bass (from published summaries). UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: the fixed 10k where the mid pot would be; all bias values; the cut control as a 6 kHz low-pass; phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage); EL84 pair at 320 V into 8k with -13 V bias (a real one is cathode biased). POWER SUPPLY: GZ34 tube rectifier plus the winding, small filter capacitor, as 170 ohm into 32 uF (supply_ohms, supply_uf on the power block), so the sag comes from the current the power tubes really draw. These two values are GUESSES from typical parts, not from this amp's schematic. (It replaced a sag block.) COUPLING: every tube stage STARTS with its coupling capacitor into its grid resistor (coupling_nf, grid_ohms; default 22 nF into 1 Mohm = 7.2 Hz; power tubes 22 nF into 220k = 33 Hz), a 1st-order high-pass, and its bias shift recovers in C x R through that same capacitor (the guessed release times are gone). The small capacitors of tight stages (0.6-2 nF, from the old 80-250 Hz high-passes) recover in 1-2 ms: that is why tight amps use them. The output transformer's low end stays a post highpass1. The cathode follower is DC-coupled to top_boost's plate (coupling_nf 0) and drives the tone stack directly; the tone stack's capacitors block the DC. PREAMP SUPPLY: every gain stage (v1, top_boost, cathode_follower, pi) hangs on the same supply through decoupling filters (preamp_targets), so it sags too, about 100 ms behind (preamp_filter_ms: a GUESS; real amps have 10k-ish resistors and 10-50 uF capacitors per node). OUTPUT TRANSFORMER: the core of a small EL84 amp's transformer, saturating on full-power notes below about 70 Hz (transformer_sat_hz: a GUESS from the amp's size, not measured): loud low notes lose bass and get odd harmonics.
